defects: THE NEW DROP-ACCOUNTING IS INCOMPLETE, and it hides exactly as many documents as it reports. Instrumenting the shipped loop on gpt2 at the study config: 100 documents seen, 17 dropped as too short (reported as _meta_phd_n_texts_too_short), 83 eligible -- and 17 MORE returned NaN and were dropped with NO field recording them (_meta_phd_n_texts = 66). Their signature: every one has 50-89 tokens, so range(50, len, 40) has exactly ONE grid point and _phd_dimension returns NaN at `len(test_n) < 2`. So phd_dimension is a mean over 66 of 100 documents while the emitted accounting explains only 17 of the 34 drops, and no warning fires for the second 17.

_meta_phd_fit_points_min = 1 is a statistic about documents that contributed NOTHING: _fit_pts is appended BEFORE the estimate is checked for finiteness, so the 17 NaN documents set the reported minimum. A 1-point OLS is not a fit at all.

The fix's own framing does not describe the shipped corpus. Its comment says 'a 200-token document is fit on 4 points and a 512-token one on 12'; measured grid-size histogram over the 83 eligible gpt2 documents is {1: 17, 2: 21, 3: 21, 4: 8, 5: 8, 6: 3, 7: 4, 8: 1} -- median 3, MAX 8, never 12, and 42 of the 66 contributing documents (64%) are slopes over just 2 or 3 grid points. The accounting was added; the unequal-weight problem it names was not addressed.

The per-document path uses `_mx = min(max_points, doc_len)` (max_points = the 2000 cloud cap) where the pooled path uses `eff_max = min(phd_max_points, n_cloud)` (phd_max_points = 512). They coincide only because max_length = 512 truncates every document; raise max_length above 512 and the two paths again use different candidate-size ceilings.

The per-document path yields nothing when dataset is None (samples = [] rather than loading the default corpus, which the pooled path does), so a dataset=None call silently reports the POOLED estimate under the name phd_dimension. _meta_phd_pooled_fallback is emitted, but the headline column changes estimand.
The per-document pass runs its own full forward pass over num_samples documents in addition to the pooled pass, roughly doubling the task's cost.
